note: Claims produced by the clean-room successor itself during Phase B and the record reconstruction. Every number is copied from a receipt file in this directory; the receipts are working-tree files until the clean-room commit lands, after which they are committed artifacts. Independent auditors for the P6 claims: DeepSeek R1 and Llama 3.3 70B via AWS Bedrock, reports under p6/audits/.

claims.statement: The sixteen P6 means in the commit message of 1e58d725 are real outputs of the committed script: a clean-room re-execution reproduces all of them to four decimals (for example CAS 0.9689, reversed 0.9272, random-fixed 0.9471, bag 0.8181 in world (a)).
claims.scope: Reproduction of the computation only. Says nothing about what the numbers mean; see CR-P6-02.
claims.independent_auditor: none needed for a reproduction; the receipt is the evidence. Both P6 auditors (p6/audits/deepseek-r1_p6_audit.md, p6/audits/llama3-3-70b_p6_audit.md) were given the raw output.
claims.notes: Before this commit the numbers existed only in the commit message (CHAT_REPORTED_ONLY on entry).

claims.statement: The committed P6 script's 'held-out' set is byte-identical to its training set for every seed and every world, because run_condition() re-draws the held-out set with the training seed (default_rng(1000 + sd)) and NTR == NTE == 1500. Every P6 accuracy is therefore a training-fit accuracy, and the script's banner '1500 train / 1500 held out' is false.
claims.scope: Checked 15 of 15 (three world functions x five seeds) before the correction was written; 20 of 20 over the four conditions by the internal reviewer; confirmed by both external auditors (A1 / Q1).
claims.independent_auditor: DeepSeek R1 (p6/audits/deepseek-r1_p6_audit.md, A1: yes) and Llama 3.3 70B (p6/audits/llama3-3-70b_p6_audit.md, Q1: yes)
claims.raw_evidence_locator: p6_order_test.py lines 160-162; p6_heldout_repro_stdout.txt 'held-out identical to train' lines; P6_RESOLUTION.md section 3
claims.known_correction: This claim IS the correction of the committed script's held-out claim.
claims.notes: Record defect CR-01. Rule for successors: assert train != held-out by array comparison before any accuracy is reported.

claims.statement: With a genuinely fresh held-out draw (seed stream 500000 + sd) and nothing else changed, every arm collapses (world (a): CAS 0.6868, reversed 0.6148, random-fixed 0.6384, bag 0.6875) and the committed script's own POSITIVE control fails (CAS 0.6868 vs bag 0.6875 in (a); reversed 0.6739 vs bag 0.6857 in (c)), so its status law returns CONTROLS_FAILED_NO_VERDICT.
claims.scope: Same arms, orders, seeds, steps, optimiser, thresholds and controls as the committed script; only the held-out draw differs. Train-fit reproduces the committed numbers 16 of 16 (positive control of the correction). Internal review: CORRECTION_SOUND; early stopping at 25-700 steps never lifts CAS above bag + 0.02.
claims.independent_auditor: DeepSeek R1 (p6/audits/deepseek-r1_p6_audit.md) P6_AUDIT_FAIL; Llama 3.3 70B (p6/audits/llama3-3-70b_p6_audit.md) P6_AUDIT_FAIL; both: SPECIFIC_CAS_ORDER_HAS_EVIDENCE_OF_VALUE: NO, GENERIC_SEQUENCING_HELPS_IN_THIS_WORLD: CANNOT_SAY
claims.raw_evidence_locator: p6_heldout_repro_stdout.txt (wall time 1 m 11.120 s); p6/audits/DISPATCH_RECEIPT.json (est. USD 0.0308 total)

claims.statement: The committed P6 headline 'BAG mechanism-free loses by 0.13-0.15 everywhere ordered' (order matters) is refuted on held-out data: the bag ties or beats every chain arm in all four worlds (held-out (a) bag 0.6875 vs best chain 0.6868; (c) 0.6857 vs 0.6739; (b) 0.4219 vs 0.3775; no-order world 0.8548 vs 0.7167).
claims.scope: At the committed operating point and, per the internal reviewer's sweep, at every step count from 25 to 700. The bag has 224 trainable parameters against 480 per chain arm, so even a bag win is a capacity-confounded comparison.
claims.independent_auditor: DeepSeek R1 and Llama 3.3 70B (both note the U = 0 capacity confound)
claims.known_correction: Withdraws the handoff line 'ordered chain vs orderless bag: sequencing appears useful in reported P6 screen'.

claims.statement: An 84-parameter least-squares reader on the flattened raw evidence beats every trained arm on held-out data in all three ordered worlds ((a) 0.7108 vs best arm 0.6875; (c) 0.7092 vs 0.6857; (b) 0.4536 vs 0.4219); the majority-class floor is 0.36-0.37, not the printed chance 0.25.
claims.scope: Same training draws (asserted equal to the committed ones) and the same fresh held-out draws as CR-P6-03. Reported first by an internal lens review, re-measured with a receipt.
claims.notes: By the standing mechanism-free-baseline rule, P6 could not have licensed an order claim even with a valid held-out set.

claims.statement: The status word CAS_PRECEDENCE_VALUE_NOT_ESTABLISHED and the sentence 'order matters, CAS ordering does not' in the commit message of 1e58d725 were NOT emitted by the program: prediction (c) FAILED, so the script took its else-branch and printed 'THE PREDICTION DID NOT HOLD AS REGISTERED ... do NOT substitute a new hypothesis for the registered one'.
claims.scope: Record fact, visible in the last three lines of the committed-script reproduction receipt. Found independently by all three internal lens reviews.
claims.raw_evidence_locator: p6_order_test.py lines 240-253; p6_committed_repro_stdout.txt last three lines
key_numbers: THE PREDICTION DID NOT HOLD AS REGISTERED
claims.notes: Record defect CR-07: status written by prose against the program's own output.

claims.statement: The specific order P > C > E > O has no evidence of value beyond any other fixed order anywhere in this arc: P6 could not test it (only 3 of 24 orders; verdict logic with no branch that could ever find it; positive control fails on held-out), and no other committed artifact claims it.
claims.scope: Never fairly tested. OPEN is not support. The older activation-based domain-precedence test (spec sheet 7.4, 2026-08-18) is PARTIAL and plausibly generic (strict fit ranks CAS 2/12 at its best layer).
claims.independent_auditor: DeepSeek R1 and Llama 3.3 70B: SPECIFIC_CAS_ORDER_HAS_EVIDENCE_OF_VALUE: NO

claims.statement: Whether generic sequencing (an ordered chain) helps on ordered worlds is OPEN: the only P6 evidence for it was training-fit, and on held-out data a mechanism-free bag and a linear rule both beat the chains.
claims.scope: P6 world family only; no other committed artifact tests it.
claims.independent_auditor: DeepSeek R1 and Llama 3.3 70B: GENERIC_SEQUENCING_HELPS_IN_THIS_WORLD: CANNOT_SAY

claims.statement: P6 (p6_order_test.py) is an invalid bench for both the specific-order and the generic-sequencing question: same-seed held-out, positive control fails once the held-out set is real, capacity-unmatched bag, labels imbalanced against a printed chance of 0.25, no registration before results, and results only in a commit message.
claims.scope: Applies to the committed script and its reported conclusion. Nothing in the original record was altered; this directory sits beside it.

claims.statement: The audit files the handoff names under REFERENCE/AUDITS/ (CJT_OHM_0R_cbffa4a0_GLM_AUDIT.md, CJT_OHM_D1_DESIGN_ATTACK_AUDIT..., PRECEDENCE_CLOSURE_AUDIT..., TRIGGER_CONFORMANCE...) do not exist at HEAD; REFERENCE/AUDITS holds only two CMB audit files. The GLM audits of the CJT lane exist only as the builder's summaries inside findings documents, spec-sheet rows and commit messages; the only committed external audit record in the lane is the DeepSeek R1 theorem audit (CJT_PREC_CLOSURE/audits/deepseek-r1_audit.md).
claims.notes: Consequence: every 'GLM audit PASS' in the lane is a builder-reported audit, not a committed audit record.

claims.statement: The CJT / CAS-Ohm lane appears in docs/CAS_HARNESS_SPEC_SHEET.md only as change-log rows (section 11, rows dated 2026-09-02) and has no capability-matrix, negatives or frontier row; the three latest lane commits (4825a37d, 61a3576d, 1e58d725) touched neither the spec sheet nor CHANGELOG.md, against the sheet's own same-commit rule.
claims.scope: Record fact at HEAD 1e58d725 (git show --stat per commit; grep of the sheet).
claims.known_correction: This clean-room commit adds a negatives entry and a change-log row for P6 and points the sheet at the ledger.

claims.statement: The DeepSeek R1 theorem audit (PRECEDENCE_THEOREM_AUDIT_PASS on the visibility law) is a committed different-family record, but its reasoning trace is example-based (it tries and fails to construct counterexamples) rather than a proof, and its verdict line names a narrower exceptional set ('positions with W_k=0 or U_k=0 downstream') than the law it certifies ('some position invisible', which also covers killed readout and saturated biases).
claims.scope: Assessment of the audit record as evidence; does not dispute the 7/7 construction test in visibility_law.py.
claims.independent_auditor: the record under assessment is itself the audit
claims.raw_evidence_locator: deepseek-r1_audit.md verdict line and reasoning trace
claims.notes: The visibility law therefore stands as: falsifiable, survived 7 constructions, one different-family audit that found no counterexample, NOT PROVED.
